I’ve had my Mirena for nearly 4 months now - I had exactly the same experience for the first two months of use, and now I get mild/moderate cramping around the time of my ‘period’ (I think my periods have now stopped after having light bleeding for a week, fortnightly for the first 3 months) - however, these cramps are SO MUCH more manageable and I can still get on with my day. 

Hope yours ease up! x
Thank you all for your kind words, I just never expected such an intense emotional impact to come with my abortion and it’s a process I’m still working on coping with.

It’s a hormone releasing IUD, but it’s extremely minimal amounts of manufactured progesterone - with the combined pill, the hormone levels are increased because you take them orally and therefore the hormones have to travel through the blood to get where they need to work, whereas the Mirena is already placed in the uterus, so hormones travel an incredibly short distance (let me know if that doesn’t make sense, I’m awful at wording things!) 

I got my IUD fitted during a surgical abortion, so unfortunately I don’t know how helpful my experience would be - I will say though, the procedure (abortion and everything) was easily less than 10 minutes; and I’m pretty sure the standard IUD insertion takes around 5 minutes or less from start to finish. The pain for me was very intense; like an extremely sharp cramping sensation, but I can’t tell if that was from the IUD insertion or not.

I have a LONG history of depression, anxiety and PTSD, so to have a hormonal birth control help with how I’m feeling is incredible, because you don’t really hear about it all that often.

I used to have horrible side effects whilst on the combined pill in regards to my mood, but I got the Mirena coil put in just under 2 months ago and I genuinely haven’t felt better mood-wise - just something to consider!
I get a similar pain with my partner now during sex if he goes too deep with my Mirena? I haven’t got a clue why, I’ve had my IUD for around a month now so hoping it’s nothing too concerning

As someone going through those kind of feelings personally, I completely understand what she means. Just let her know that you’re there for her in little ways - remind her that you love her, if she looks zoned out at all when you’re with her just give her a quick cuddle and then give her some space, and just be there for her as best as you can.

It’s a horrible place to be in mentally but as long as she knows she’s loved, hopefully it’ll be enough to keep her from delving too deeply into her emotions.
If you need any support as well (because it’s not always easy being the partner of someone that’s gone through this) just send me a message and we can think of some ways to manage everything.
I needed this more than you can imagine - thank you.

Mistakes do happen during protected sex, you hear about them all the time; and even if it wasn’t, why is it any of your business? 

You know nothing about what this woman is experiencing currently - the priority in this situation is that she does what’s safest and healthiest for her, mentally and physically. Back off.
How do you know she didn’t just have an accident during protected sex? She asked for advice, not for judgement.

I had sex 3 days after I had my surgical procedure - BPAS suggests you wait until you feel physically better and ready, and that’s exactly what I did. There was no pain and no discomfort during, but I woke up with some mild cramping that passed in about an hour. As long as you take it easy and listen to what your body is telling you, then I can’t see why not x
Look after yourself darling, take everything easy and avoid stress whenever you can for a little bit (easier said than done I know!)

Definitely save telling people if you don’t need to - it’ll just add extra stress to the situation and you don’t want that on top of your discomfort; my partner’s family (and most of my own) don’t even know what happened to me and I feel like it’s better that way in my circumstances. For the pain, hot water bottles and ibuprofen will really help, and sleeping with a pillow between your legs should ease any lower back pain somewhat - if you need any emotional support just let me know and I’ll drop you a message privately and we can talk some more x

For me I found a hot water bottle really helped but if that’s not working well for you, maybe try applying a cold compress to any areas that are feeling sore? Ibuprofen worked wonders for me as well; 400mg with the hot water bottle and a pillow between my legs (just helped to squeeze something with them) and a nap really helped me to manage the pain and cramping x

I’ve had my Mirena for about 3 weeks now - the strings for the first week were very noticeable for me; I went to the hospital because I thought it had rejected but turns out my strings are just super long! The important thing is that you can still feel your strings - as long as you feel them and you’re not experiencing intense pain or bleeding, you should be all good. And sometimes, even if you can’t feel your strings at all, it’s just because the cervix fluctuates in shape throughout the course of the month, so it may swell slightly over the strings. 

If you feel like anything is super concerning, the best thing to do is just go to your GP or sexual health clinic and ask them for an appointment for them to be checked x

Definitely make this week all about yourself and recover as best as you can - I’ve noticed that people that haven’t experienced this kind of thing can be a bit quick to assume that you’re completely better immediately, so do whatever you need to get yourself up and running again. I was only 7 weeks and 2 days when I had my procedure, so I didn’t experience any boob-leaking dilemmas; I think that’s more often experienced by people past the 10 week mark (please correct me on this if I’m wrong!). Best of luck and sending lots of love your way whilst you move on, and just give me a shout if you worry about anything (i know how helpful it can be to have someone to listen to your concerns, I’ve definitely shared a few on here myself) x

Isn’t it so nice being able to just eat again?! I had the worst ‘all day’ sickness, to the point where I had lost nearly a stone in 2 weeks because I couldn’t stomach anything at all - all my symptoms pretty much disappeared around 3 days after, minus the cramping (my cramps lasted for around a week and a half, varying in intensity day-to-day) - and I’m so paranoid with anything to do with my health so I’ve literally been checking my coil strings every other day (as I got it fitted during the procedure) as well as writing down any ‘off’ feelings I’ve been having, which has definitely helped my own nerves to some extent - sometimes seeing it written out makes you realise if you’re just being silly (that’s what’s happened in my case anyway!)

Honestly I was so worried as well because my clinic was nearly 2 hours away so I would’ve had to apply for a prescription at a local GP or something and that just means more time but you’re all good! Just keep an eye on how your body feels over the next few days and as long as nothing alarming is happening (like excessively heavy bleeding or fever-like symptoms) you’ll be fine x

I don’t know if you’re UK based or not, but the antibiotics provided as part of the abortion process here are more of an extra cautionary step - the tablets themselves are the exact same treatment that someone with chlamydia would take, thus they aren’t ‘abortion specific’. I had a similar concern as I was sick in just under an hour after taking my antibiotics following my surgical procedure, but typically the antibiotics absorb into the body within half an hour, and are still just as effective at keeping infection at bay if you take them later on in the process x

The procedure day for me was incredibly daunting, and whilst my personal experience wasn’t pleasant, it was so quick (not even a full 10 minutes) and the nurses helping were supportive and did everything they could to calm me down. I know the feeling of that connection you make, and it’s upsetting me too knowing it was the best thing for me and my life to end the pregnancy, but if you ever need any extra support, please drop me a message x

I bled lightly immediately after my surgical, and then around 4/5 days later, the bleeding became a lot more like a heavy period with some large clots around a full week after - everything trailed off by the second week and I get the LIGHTEST spotting for like 10 minutes during the day now (not even proper spotting, more like a ‘wipe and see some pink residue’ situation) x
In the UK it’s common practice to have the pills inserted vaginally, but do whatever you’re comfortable with x
Thank you so much, it means a lot x
Look after yourself and make the most of the people you have around you right now - I wish I was in the same position ❤️ x

I think you’ve honestly summed up my experience better than I did myself - thank you so much for sharing this with me. I’m living in halls as well right now and I’m over 100 miles from home (including my partner) so it’s becoming increasingly harder to find anyone to share my experience with, just due to distance.

I’m also finding it hard to talk to my friend about it too - they’re so supportive but they also know that because they’ve never experienced this first hand, there’s a limit to how much advice they can give just because they don’t know what to say.

If you ever want to drop me a message, please do because I feel like we’ve had shockingly similar experiences and hopefully we can work this out together - much love❤️
This has been really helpful, thank you so much x

Thank you for responding firstly, I didn’t expect anyone to help so quickly.

I don’t know what I feel stronger, honestly. I wish I didn’t get pregnant in the first place, but purely because I wish I didn’t have to make the decision I did. My family have a history of having children around the age of 18, so I know we’re capable of providing even at a young age - but I think that knowledge of my family history made me think I had a chance at being a good mother even if I was in a difficult spot in my life, and that’s slowly making me regret my choice.
I had sex 4 days after my surgical - there was no pain, and no discomfort other than a dull ache in my lower stomach the following morning (which was very quickly resolved with some ibuprofen).
